policy: Antipatris has a page of its own, at the same point on the map as Aphek: Herod the Great rebuilt Aphek of the Sharon and named it Antipatris. Each page says so of the other.
source: Essenthos, on the project owner's decision of 2026-10-29 that Antipatris, Herod's rebuilding of Aphek, keeps a page of its own

says.notes: The town Herod the Great rebuilt on the site of Aphek and named after his father Antipater; it stands where Aphek stood (1SA 4:1).

rulings.why: 'Then the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul, and brought him by night to Antipatris' (ACT 23:31).

says.notes: Herod the Great later rebuilt the town on this site and named it Antipatris, after his father Antipater (ACT 23:31).

rulings.why: 'And the Philistines pitched in Aphek' (1SA 4:1): Aphek of the Sharon, on whose site Herod built Antipatris.
